sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4,860.4 million in FY2016 to $14,342.9 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
The path was a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue jumped 89.1% in FY2021 to $16,071.7 million, then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12,172.9 million [D241][F6][D292][F7].
REGEN-COV contributed 66.4pp of the FY2021 increase and its disappearance cost 36.3pp in FY2022 [D582][D585], with the FY2022 decline tied to the end of those U.S. product sales [P33].
Operating margin peaked at 55.7% in FY2021 and has fallen every year since, to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30][R1].
In FY2025 collaboration revenue grew 21.0% and contributed 9.0pp of the 1.0% total revenue growth, while net product sales fell 17.3% and subtracted 9.3pp [D522][D523][D440][D506][D507].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits rose 33.6% and added 9.3pp, driven by higher Dupixent sales [D591][D592][P9].
U.S. EYLEA net product sales fell 42.4% and subtracted 14.2pp, on lower volumes from competitive pressure and the EYLEA HD transition plus a lower net selling price [D577][D578][P10].
Operating costs grew 4.4pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 5.4% against 1.0% [D464][D457][D440].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% against net income growth of 2.1%, as the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D444][D442][D459].
The FY2025 operating margin of 24.9% is the window low, 9.7pp below the 34.6% median and 30.8pp below the 55.7% high [F30][D749][D751][F26][D750].
R&D took 4.7pp off the FY2025 operating margin as it rose to 40.8% of revenue, while SG&A added 2.0pp as it fell 8.6% [D465][D420][D466][D456].
The SG&A decline was primarily due to lower charitable contributions to Good Days [P5].
In FY2025 net margin of 31.4% sat 6.5pp above the 24.9% operating margin, as other income of $1,652.8 million offset tax expense of $725.8 million [F50][F30][D797][X117][X107].
FY2025 operating cash flow of $4,978.9 million was 1.11x net income, against a window median of 1.10x [F80][F40][D428][D787].
Free cash flow of $4,080.5 million was 0.91x net income and a 28.4% margin, above the 26.4% window median [F100][F40][D429][D425][D757].
Capex of $898.4 million was 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A of $543.7 million [F90][F10][D424][D430][X67].
Stock-based compensation of $993.7 million equalled 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][F80][D431].
Cash and investments reached $18,865.8 million in FY2025 against total debt of $1,985.9 million, a net cash position of $16,879.9 million [D432][D433][D434].
That is net cash of 117.7% of revenue, in the 100th percentile of eight biopharma peers against a -50.7% median [D435][D780][D781].
Buybacks of $3,438.6 million plus dividends of $370.3 million absorbed 93.3% of free cash flow in FY2025 [X137][X140][D436][D437].
Return on average equity fell to 14.9%, in the 25th percentile of eight peers against a 38.7% median [D439][D784][D785].
Operating margin has fallen four straight years, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30][R1].
The decline now sits at the window low, so the margin base is materially smaller than the one the cash returns were built on [F30][D749].
FY2018 revenue is shown as $5,145.6 million against $6,710.8 million first reported, and FY2019 as $6,557.6 million against $7,863.4 million [F3][X3][F4][X4][R2].
Growth and margins spanning those recast years mix two presentations, so the FY2018 decline of 12.4% should not be read as a like-for-like move [D92][R2].
Whether U.S. EYLEA net product sales, $2,747.8 million in FY2025, fall further or stabilise, in the FY2026 10-K [S43].
Whether the operating margin, 24.9% in FY2025, recovers toward the 34.6% window median or sets a new low, in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D751].
Whether R&D stays above the 40.8% of revenue recorded in FY2025 or falls back toward the 34.6% median, in the FY2026 10-K [D420][D760].
